equations.description: A first-order linear ordinary differential equation involving the derivative of y with respect to t, and the product of t and y.
The initial condition for the differential equation, stating that the value of y is 3 when t is 0.
The first-order linear ordinary differential equation multiplied by an integrating factor U.
The derivative of the product of U and y with respect to t, representing the desired form of the left-hand side of the differential equation after applying an integrating factor.
A derived differential equation for the integrating factor U, where U dot is the derivative of U with respect to t.
The integrating factor U, calculated as the exponential of the indefinite integral of t.

The differential equation rewritten with the integrating factor, where the left side is the derivative of the product U times y and the right side is t multiplied by e to the power of t squared over 2.
Both sides of the differential equation are integrated with respect to t to solve for y.
The result of integrating both sides of the modified differential equation, including the constant of integration C.
The general solution for y as a function of t, obtained by dividing by the integrating factor U and simplifying.
The initial condition y of 0 equals 3 applied to the general solution to solve for the constant C.
The value of the constant of integration C found from the initial condition.
The definite integral form of the modified differential equation, with integration limits from 0 to t and using a dummy variable s for integration.
The result of evaluating the definite integrals on both sides, expressing the difference of Uy at t and 0, and showing the evaluation of the exponential function at t and 0.
The values of the integrating factor U at t=0 and the initial condition for y at t=0.
The solution for y derived using definite integrals, before final simplification.
